problem: Describe the situation before your work: what was slow, broken, or manual. Keep it concrete — queues, lost forms, hours wasted. One or two short paragraphs.
What made it hard? A constraint, a legacy process, a tight deadline. This is where the reader starts rooting for you.
solution: What you built, in plain language. Who uses it, what they can do now, and the one design/engineering decision you're proudest of.
Mention your role honestly — solo, or which parts were yours in a team.

process.title: Research
process.text: Interviewed the office staff and students; mapped the paper flow before designing anything.

process.title: Design
process.text: Wireframes in Figma, tested with five students, two rounds of revisions.

process.title: Build
process.text: React front end, Node/Express API, MySQL. Weekly progress links to the stakeholders.

process.title: Ship
process.text: Deployed, wrote a one-page admin guide, trained the staff in one session.

changed: The result in the user's terms: time saved, errors gone, people served. If you have a quote from the client or adviser, this is where it lives.
next: One honest paragraph on limitations or the next iteration. This reads as maturity, not weakness.
